title: SVM + RBF Kernel Trick
subtitle: 3D Radial Lifting & Maximum-Margin Hyperplane
summary: Lift non-linear 2D concentric rings into 3D space (z = x² + y²) so a flat hyperplane separates them.

evaluationChart.title: Hinge Loss & Margin Width vs. Regularization C
evaluationChart.description: Illustrates how larger C tightens margin violations (lower hinge loss) at the cost of narrower margin width.

advantages: Kernel trick captures complex non-linear boundaries without explicit high-dim coordinates.
Maximum-margin objective yields strong generalization on small-to-medium datasets.
Memory-efficient at inference: depends only on Support Vectors.
limitations: Training scales poorly (O(n²) to O(n³)) on very large datasets.
Does not natively output calibrated probabilities.
Sensitive to kernel hyperparameters (gamma, C) and feature scaling.

codeTemplates.fromScratch:
import numpy as np

def radial_lift(X):
    z = np.sum(X ** 2, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    return np.hstack([X, z])

# Inner ring vs outer ring in 2D
X_inner = np.random.randn(20, 2) * 0.4
X_outer = np.random.randn(20, 2) * 0.3 + np.array([2.0, 0.0])
X_3d = radial_lift(np.vstack([X_inner, X_outer]))
print('Lifted 3D shape:', X_3d.shape)
codeTemplates.scikitLearn:
from sklearn.svm import SVC
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[0.3,0.2],[-0.4,0.3],[1.9,0.4],[-1.8,0.6]])
y = np.array([1, 1, -1, -1])

clf = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), SVC(kernel='rbf', C=2.5, gamma='scale'))
clf.fit(X, y)
print('Support vectors:', clf.named_steps['svc'].n_support_)
